iPhone: open the schedule straight from Mail

Add a Shortcut once. After that, open the schedule PDF in Mail, tap Share, and tap the shortcut. This page opens; tap Paste from Shortcut, then Paste, and your week appears. The Shortcut hands the PDF over through your clipboard, so it stays on your phone and nothing is uploaded.

Already made the shortcut? Edit its Text step so it's only https://jza103.github.io/shift-finder/#paste: delete the Base64 Encoded bubble and change #pdf= to #paste. Nothing else needs to change.

Get the shortcut Tap Add Shortcut and you're set; skip the steps below. In the share sheet, look for the name it showed when you added it.

Or build it yourself:

  1. Open the Shortcuts app and tap + to start a new shortcut. Tap its name at the top and rename it Shift Finder.
  2. Search the actions for Base64 Encode and add it. Tap the blue Input word in it and choose Shortcut Input.
  3. A block appears at the very top that reads Receive Any input from Nowhere. Tap Nowhere, check Share Sheet, and tap Done. Optionally tap Any and leave only PDFs on, so the shortcut only shows up for PDFs.
  4. Add Copy to Clipboard. It fills in Base64 Encoded by itself.
  5. Add Text and type https://jza103.github.io/shift-finder/#paste
  6. Add Open URLs. It fills in Text by itself. Tap Done.

To use it: open the email, tap the PDF, tap Share, and scroll to the bottom of the list to tap the shortcut. If it isn't listed, tap Edit Actions… at the bottom and add it. The first time, tap Allow when it asks to open the link. On the page, tap Paste from Shortcut, then the Paste bubble your iPhone shows.

No “Nowhere” block? Look for the shortcut's Details: tap the name at the top, or the ⓘ or ⋯ button. Turn on Show in Share Sheet there.

The page remembers the last name you picked, so after the first time your week shows up as soon as you paste.

Tap a shift to see who else is on it and who could take it if you give it away. Locations come from the slanted column headers. Checks flag cells that don't match their column, typo-looking times, and a.m./p.m. that had to be assumed.
